newsitem.title: UK: Specials ease off in UK gilt repo market.
newsitem.headline: Specials ease off in UK gilt repo market.

text.p: The gilt repo market had to content itself with only two special stocks on Wednesday and even they traded only modestly through general collateral rates, dealers said.
The 8.0 percent gilts due 2003 traded about 35 to 40 basis points through GC at two weeks. The 7.0 percents of 2001 achieved a similar level of expense out to two weeks.

But that pales in comparison with recent special stocks such as the 6.0 percent gilts due 1999 which less than two weeks ago were trading at around 1.5 percent overnight, some 400 basis points through GC.
Two-week GC was quoted at 5.80/5.70 percent in late trade on Wednesday.
"There are specials still running with the 7s of '01 and 8.0s of 2003 but the 6.0 percents of 1999 have lost their flavour altogether now," one gilt repo trader said.
He said general collateral rates had pushed up through the session, with the Bank of England unable to take out a modest shortage in full.
"We saw overnight GC around 5.75/70 early on and then pushing up to 6.00 percent and above," the trader said.
The Bank of England forecast a 700 million stg money market shortage early on Wednesday, later revising that up to 750 million.
Yet even with 325 million stg of unspecified late assistance, the Bank had only managed to take out 535 million stg of that shortage by the close of play.
"There's been a distinct lack of interest in selling paper today," one money market trader said. "Everyone's given up on the idea of cheaper money."
With Wednesday's shortage left partly outstanding, the trader said unsecured overnight money market rates had pushed up to around 6-1/2 percent or even seven percent.
"There's money changing hands at that level as we speak."
Compare that with Tuesday when an 850 million stg shortage was taken out in full. Then, overnight cash was quoted as low as 2-1/2 percent in late business, below Monday's levels around 5-13/16 3/4.
The trader said there may not be much light on the horizon.
"Thursday's tend to be equally awkward as people save their paper for what they hope will be a cheaper weekend."
